title: Rank ladder race
materials: Army insignia cards per patrol: enlisted (E-1 to E-9) and officer (O-1 to O-10)

displayContent.headline: Rank ladder race
displayContent.body: Tape the insignia cards on the wall in order, lowest to highest. Two ladders: enlisted E-1 to E-9, and officers O-1 to O-10.

prompts.text: Gold or silver: which ranks higher?
prompts.answer: Silver. A second lieutenant’s gold bar is below a first lieutenant’s silver bar, and a major’s gold oak leaf is below a lieutenant colonel’s silver oak leaf.

prompts.text: What’s the difference between an officer and a sergeant?
prompts.answer: Officers hold a commission (from an academy, ROTC or officer school), need a college degree, and plan and lead. NCOs are enlisted soldiers who rose through the ranks; they train and lead soldiers day to day.

leaderScript: Each patrol races to tape both ladders on the wall.
Press → for the answer key and R to show it while you score.
Press → for the gotcha question everyone misses: gold ranks below silver.
Ask: in our troop, who’s more like an officer, and who’s more like a sergeant?
If a boy asks about warrant officers: W-1 to W-5 are technical experts, ranked above enlisted soldiers and below second lieutenants.

discussionQuestions.question: In our troop, who’s more like an officer, and who’s more like a sergeant?
discussionQuestions.answer: Open question; there’s no answer key.

ifShortOnTime: This is the first block to cut: capture the flag needs its full 30 minutes. If you keep it, race the officer ladder only.
